name: Mercy-Shallows
geological_features: Planet-wide shallow seas averaging only 200 meters depth
Sandbars and atolls forming intricate archipelago chains
description: Mercy-Shallows is an oceanic world of remarkable gentleness, its seas nowhere deeper than a few hundred meters and its surface broken by thousands of sandy atolls and winding archipelagoes. The water runs warm and clear as glass, revealing a seabed carpeted in pastel-colored organisms that sway in the mild currents.

The breathable atmosphere carries the clean salt smell of healthy ocean, and the low gravity lends a buoyancy to movement that makes traversing the shallows feel like flight. Sunsets here last for hours, the sky cycling through impossible shades of rose and gold reflected in the mirror-still lagoons.

No predators larger than a human hand have been catalogued in Mercy-Shallows' ecosystems, an evolutionary anomaly that has puzzled xenobiologists for decades. The fauna display no fight-or-flight responses to unfamiliar stimuli, suggesting a world where competition evolved along cooperative rather than adversarial lines.

The planet has become an unofficial sanctuary for trauma survivors and veterans across the sector, its gentle environment and absence of threat providing therapeutic benefits that no artificial facility can replicate. Proposals to establish formal medical retreats here face opposition from conservationists who fear that even benign colonization could disrupt the delicate ecological balance.
